text:
The unemployment rate of 5.8% and fed funds at 0.10% point to late 2014. Headline CPI of 1.65% fits a falling oil price, and the dollar up 6% over the past 3 months fits the autumn 2014 rally. Gold is down about 15.8% from its 12-month high, which fits as well.

Candidates are October and November 2014. The unemployment rate was 5.9% in September, 5.8% in October and 5.8% in November. The 3-month change of -0.4 compares against 6.2% in July (October minus July = -0.4), which supports October. Headline CPI for October 2014 was 1.7%, and November was 1.3%, so 1.65 fits October. The 10-year yield was 2.24% at the end of October. US large-cap equity returned +4.6% in October 2014, and the VIX was about 14, though the 12.07 figure may be a different measure. Developed ex-US returned +2.6% in the month, which is consistent with a rebound from the October low. Gold fell 3.7% in October 2014, consistent as well.

October 2014 is the best fit.
